extraction.name: C-E VAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models
extraction.description: C-E VAL is the first comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context. It comprises 13948 multiple-choice questions across four difficulty levels (middle school, high school, college, and professional) and 52 diverse disciplines, ranging from humanities to science and engineering. It also includes C-E VAL HARD, a subset of very challenging subjects requiring advanced reasoning. The suite is constructed from real-world, challenging human exams in China.
extraction.creator: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He
extraction.publisher: 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023) Track on Datasets and Benchmarks.
extraction.citeAs: Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Chuancheng Lv, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He. In 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023) Track on Datasets and Benchmarks, 2023.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The C-E VAL dataset was constructed from real-world, challenging human exams in China. Questions were collected from mock exams freely available on the internet, past exam questions from top universities in China publicly shared by students, and a minor fraction of mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam from the Weipu website (with authorization for inclusion). The questions cover four difficulty levels: middle school, high school, college, and professional, spanning 52 diverse disciplines.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Mock exams freely available on the internet, past exam questions from top universities in China publicly shared by students, and mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam from the Weipu website.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions with fewer than four options were eliminated. For questions with more than four options, incorrect choices were randomly dropped to ensure all questions have exactly four choices.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Collected data, primarily in PDF or Microsoft Word documents and some web pages, were initially processed into text. All questions were then parsed into a structured format, automatically when possible, and manually by the authors otherwise. Complex mathematical notations were manually converted into standard LATEX formats. The data underwent deduplication and cleaning. Finally, questions were human-validated by the authors in several rounds to ensure LATEX notation compliance and overall quality. Questions were split into development, validation, and test sets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For the development split, explanations for the ground-truth answers were generated. This involved first prompting GPT-4 to generate step-by-step explanations, which were then manually revised by the authors (Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, and Junxian He) to obtain the final high-quality explanations. The initial data collection also involved 'some necessary manual annotation from PDF or Word documents' by the authors to obtain the final structured format.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: One ground-truth answer per question. For the development split, one explanation per question was generated and manually revised.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: The authors of the paper (Yuzhen Huang, Yuzhuo Bai, Zhihao Zhu, Junlei Zhang, Jinghan Zhang, Tangjun Su, Junteng Liu, Yikai Zhang, Jiayi Lei, Yao Fu, Maosong Sun, Junxian He) were involved in manual annotation and revision.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used to automatically generate initial step-by-step explanations for the development split, which were then manually revised.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Ground-truth labels for the development and validation splits are released. Labels for the test split are kept private, requiring users to submit model predictions to https://cevalbenchmark.com for automatic evaluation and inclusion in a public leaderboard. No explicit versioning or deprecation policies are mentioned beyond this submission system.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to help analyze important strengths and shortcomings of foundation models, foster their development and growth for Chinese users, and guide developers in preparing LLMs to function in more complex scenarios beyond casual conversational bots.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper acknowledges that English benchmarks tend to exhibit geographical biases towards the domestic knowledge of the regions that produce them, and C-E VAL aims to address this by focusing on Chinese context, culture, history, and laws. The paper also discusses 'option bias' in the distribution of correct answers, noting that while there are fluctuations, they are relatively small around a random 25% level and similar to MMLU. Experiments with permuted choices showed small variance, suggesting limited option bias impact on models.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: C-E VAL, along with all English-language benchmarks, is acknowledged as 'far from perfect for LLM evaluation'. The authors note that there are many other abilities such as reasoning over and calling APIs, as well as multiple aspects that extend beyond accuracy, including safety, bias, and robustness, which are left for future exploration.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The development set (five exemplars per subject) is intended for few-shot evaluation and few-shot chain-of-thought settings. The validation set is for hyperparameter tuning. The test set is for final evaluation, with predictions submitted to the official website for scoring. The dataset is intended to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models, analyze their strengths and shortcomings, and guide their development for Chinese users.
